text: Judge any combinator that selects or reorders records first by the order of the reads it causes, then by what it allocates. The target regime is MGnify: about 2.456 billion records over about 500 GB, with draws often in the billions. A 19.6 GB index vector is a cost Jack pays without complaint; billions of seeks across half a terabyte is not. Sampling is where this bites: a sample is a set, and ascending file order makes its reads sequential.
